extracted.intended_audience: annotators and NLP/humor researchers building or evaluating cartoon captioning systems
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for annotating and evaluating humorous captions for cartoons, including creating short joke explanations, labeling image elements and incongruities, and tasks for matching, ranking, and explanation generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke explanation (brief, friend-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In a few sentences, explain the joke as if to a friend who doesn't 'get it' yet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a short (the corpus average ~60 words) explanation that makes the punchline comprehensible to someone who didn't get it; explain why it's funny rather than merely restating the caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image description
rubrics_metrics.description: Literal scene, locations, entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators should provide a straightforward, literal description of the cartoon's visible elements to ground later explanation and linking to the caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncanny / unusual elements
rubrics_metrics.description: What is incongruous in the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify odd, unexpected, or incongruous aspects of the image that the caption might exploit; these elements are central to linking image and caption humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Why the winning caption is funny, connecting unusual elements to the punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the caption leverages the image's unusual elements (or external knowledge) to produce humor; connect incongruity to an explanatory frame for the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perplexity / surprisingness
rubrics_metrics.description: Perplexity (under a language model) — surprisingness predicts humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower probability / higher surprisingness under a language model is a predictive feature of funny captions; can be used as a quantitative signal for identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match to image setting and uncanniness
rubrics_metrics.description: Caption must engage what's weird: match to image setting and uncanniness description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good captions specifically reference or exploit the image's setting or its identified uncanny elements; alignment between caption content and image incongruity is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Short, simple, clear language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions (and explanations) should be concise and easily readable; clarity and brevity help comedic effect and annotator understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper nouns / specific named entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of proper nouns — specific named entities help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including specific names or concrete referents can increase perceived funniness or specificity; annotate presence of proper nouns as a useful feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-centeredness (WordNet 'person'/'relative' overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlap with WordNet's 'person' and 'relative' synsets — human-centeredness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions focusing on people/relations tend to be funnier in this dataset; measure overlap with person-centric synsets as a signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical centrality with uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexical centrality among submissions — but unique enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective captions strike a balance: they are lexically central (relate to what others submit) while retaining some uniqueness; measure centrality among candidate captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment / appropriate emotional tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment — appropriate emotional tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The emotional tone of the caption should be appropriate for the joke; sentiment analysis can be used to check alignment with expected comedic tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect / playful image-caption relationships (challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect, playful image-caption relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions often relate to the image in non-literal, indirect ways; evaluators and models must handle implicature, inference, and playful mappings rather than one-to-one descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to real-world entities and norms (challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference real-world entities and norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good captions frequently rely on knowledge of real-world entities, cultural norms, or conventions; lack of such knowledge can block understanding or generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory-of-mind reasoning (challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theory-of-mind reasoning about characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions may require attributing mental states, intentions, or beliefs to characters; explanations should capture plausible interiors or motivations when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural context required (challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural context required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some jokes require specific cultural knowledge; annotators should note when cultural references are necessary and models must be evaluated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdworker explanation difficulty (empirical note)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Several attempts to solicit explanations from crowdworkers were not satisfactory."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that off-the-shelf crowdworker elicitation may fail; provide clear instructions/examples and expect that explanation elicitation is nontrivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching task (caption-to-cartoon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching: caption-to-cartoon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An evaluation/annotation task where captions are paired to cartoons; measures whether caption content properly aligns to the correct image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality ranking task
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Ranking: finalist > low-quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators rank captions by quality (e.g., finalists versus low-quality submissions); used for learning-to-rank or evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation generation task
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation: generate joke explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task to produce the short explanatory text (as in the 'Joke explanation' guideline); used to evaluate whether a model can make the humor explicit and coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the caption engage the image's unusual element?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item 1: "Does the caption engage the image's unusual element?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct check of whether the caption references or leverages the image's identified incongruity; central for judging relevance of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does it provide a coherent explanation/frame for the absurd?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item 2: "Does it provide a coherent explanation/frame for the absurd?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the caption establishes or implies a plausible frame that makes the absurdity sensible and thus funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does it ascribe a believable interior to a character?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item 3: "Does it ascribe a believable interior to a character?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the caption implies believable thoughts, feelings, or motivations for characters, enabling theory-of-mind reasoning in the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is it readable, with appropriate sentiment?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item 4: "Is it readable, with appropriate sentiment?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for clarity, concision, and that the sentiment/emotional tone matches the intended humor rather than being confusing or off-putting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Could one explain in 60 words why it's funny?
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric item 5: "Could one explain in 60 words why it's funny?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verifies that the joke's mechanisms are explicable in a brief explanation (approx. 60 words); this is both a verbosity guideline and a proxy for explainability.
